basic_identification.name: Runtime art / NFTs-as-software
basic_identification.originator: Material Protocol Arts (studio, notably Cycles project); Mathcastles (Terraforms, foundational); Pak (protocol art via smart contracts); 0xDEAFBEEF (on-chain audiovisual); broader movement includes many generative art practitioners working with fully on-chain, executable code
basic_identification.geography: Global; primarily Ethereum ecosystem; studios and individual practitioners distributed internationally

core_ideas.core_claim: NFTs that function as executable software rather than static images — live-running programs on the blockchain where the protocol itself is the artwork, not any single rendered output. The token is a program, not a picture. Ownership means owning running code, not a file. As blockchain infrastructure matures, NFTs encode logic, change state, respond to conditions, and compute in real time.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Maximally medium-specific. Runtime art is impossible outside of blockchain and computing infrastructure. The work IS code executing on a virtual machine. Static images are side effects of computation, not the art itself. On-chain storage means the art exists as long as the blockchain exists, computed from first principles without external dependencies. This is the strongest case for digital art's medium specificity — the artwork is a process, not an object.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Resists attention economy through complexity and duration. Runtime art requires engagement with code, computation, and process — not glanceable images. Terraforms and Cycles demand sustained exploration rather than quick consumption. The aesthetic reward comes from understanding the system, not consuming a visual product. However, the spectacle of 'art that runs on Ethereum' generates attention-economy coverage (tech media, crypto press). The conceptual innovation attracts attention even as the practice resists it.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Strongly intention-native. Runtime art declares a structural position about what digital art can be — executable code rather than static file. This is an infrastructure-level artistic statement. The intention is to prove that tokens can be programs, that ownership can mean owning process, and that permanence can be guaranteed through on-chain computation. This serves the field's need for medium-specific practice rather than capturing engagement.

market_economics.revenue_model: Primary sales of NFT editions. Secondary market trading with creator royalties. Material Protocol Arts' Cycles: 512 editions (lenses), floor price ~$951. No subscription or recurring revenue. Some projects use on-chain mechanics for ongoing interaction (minting, burning, transforming). The studio model (Material Protocol Arts) allows pooled resources rather than individual artist economics.
market_economics.market_position: Niche primary and secondary market. Positioned as the conceptual frontier of on-chain art. Competes with generative art platforms (Art Blocks, fxhash) but distinguishes itself through fully on-chain computation rather than off-chain rendering. Collectors are buying conceptual innovation as much as visual output.
market_economics.price_range: Cycles floor: ~$951 per lens (484 minted, 229 owners, ~$460K total market cap). Terraforms by Mathcastles: floor varies but historically 0.2-2 ETH. Pak's protocol works: wide range from accessible editions to multi-million dollar sales. 0xDEAFBEEF: individual works at auction-level prices. Overall niche market with dedicated but small collector base. [uncertain]
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Stable niche. Not experiencing the volume surge or crash of broader NFT market — operates in a conceptual art space with dedicated collectors. The academic attention (arXiv papers, 2025 ARTECH conference) suggests growing intellectual interest even as market volumes remain modest. The concept is growing in influence even if transaction volume is flat.
market_economics.collector_demographics: Highly technical crypto-native collectors who value code, computation, and conceptual innovation. Strong overlap with generative art collector community (Art Blocks, fxhash). Institutional interest from digital art-focused collections. Not accessible to non-crypto collectors. Very small community — Cycles has 229 unique owners. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: Moderate. The on-chain nature means the art persists as long as the blockchain persists, providing aesthetic sustainability. Market sustainability depends on continued collector interest in conceptual innovation. The studio model (Material Protocol Arts) spreads financial risk. No recurring revenue mechanisms. Sustainability is cultural (the ideas persist) rather than financial (limited market).

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Solidity smart contracts for on-chain computation. JavaScript/p5.js for rendering (Cycles). EVM as execution environment. Ethereum mainnet for storage and computation. SVG generation on-chain (some projects). WebGL/Three.js for 3D rendering. The key constraint is gas costs and EVM computation limits — artists must optimize code for on-chain efficiency.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Largely orthogonal. Runtime art is about human-written code executed deterministically — the opposite of probabilistic AI generation. The practice emphasizes authorship, craftsmanship, and intentional programming rather than emergent AI outputs. AI could potentially be incorporated (an on-chain AI model as runtime art) but this has not been the primary direction. The movement implicitly argues for human programming as creative practice in an age of AI generation.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Maximally live. The art is continuously computed on the blockchain. Cycles is described as a 'moving, abstract kinetic sculpture dynamically computed on Ethereum.' The artwork exists as running process, not stored file. Some works change state based on blockchain events (block numbers, transactions, time). This is the most radically live form of digital art.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Rapidly developing and highly technical: 'on-chain computation,' 'protocol art,' 'smart contract aesthetics,' 'gas-optimized code,' 'deterministic rendering,' 'SDF (Signed Distance Function),' 'EVM as medium,' 'blockchain-native.' The 2025 arXiv paper on Pak's protocol art contributes academic vocabulary. The language borrows from software engineering and computer science but is being adapted for art-critical purposes. A 2025 ARTECH conference paper theorizes 'protocol as poetry.'
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Openness: open (code is on-chain, verifiable, inspectable by anyone). Commons vs. capture: leans commons (on-chain code is a public good by nature; smart contracts are immutable and open). Spectacle vs. infrastructure: infrastructure masquerading as spectacle — the art IS the infrastructure (running code). Individual vs. collective: primarily individual artists/studios, but on-chain code invites permissionless interaction and extension.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Maximally open. On-chain code is publicly verifiable and readable. Smart contracts are immutable and transparent. SVG outputs include the full code needed for reproduction. The art medium (Ethereum) is itself open infrastructure. This is among the most open art practices possible.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Smart contract governance — the code defines the rules, and the rules are immutable once deployed. No curatorial gatekeeping for individual projects. Studio governance (Material Protocol Arts) for collaborative works. No DAO or community governance at the movement level. The blockchain itself is the governance layer.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Strong. Art and code are on-chain — owned by no centralized entity. NFT holders own their specific tokens. The code is public and permanent. No platform can remove or modify deployed smart contracts. This is the strongest data sovereignty model in digital art.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: High. Standard ERC-721 NFTs — compatible with all Ethereum infrastructure. On-chain code can be read by any compatible system. Smart contract interactions are composable. Other contracts can interact with runtime art contracts. This is infrastructure-level interoperability.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: The strongest in digital art. On-chain code persists as long as Ethereum persists. No dependency on IPFS, external servers, or platform survival. The art can be reconstructed from blockchain data alone. The vulnerability is JavaScript runtime environment changes over decades — but the code itself is permanently preserved.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Code-defined. Smart contracts define who can interact and how. Permissionless viewing (anyone can see on-chain code). Gated interaction (only token holders can trigger certain functions). No machine-readable consent for downstream use beyond what the smart contract encodes. The immutability of smart contracts means consent architecture is fixed at deployment.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Parallel with growing intellectual recognition. Academic papers (arXiv, ARTECH) bridge the gap. Conceptual art discourse recognizes protocol art as extending conceptual and process art traditions (Sol LeWitt, Fluxus). But market integration with traditional galleries/museums is minimal. The work is too technically demanding for most traditional art world institutions to exhibit or collect.
field_position.what_it_enables: Art that exists permanently without any external dependency. Code as creative medium with provenance guaranteed by blockchain. Ownership of running processes, not static files. Composable art — other smart contracts can interact with runtime art. The proof that tokens can be programs, not just receipts for files. A new category of medium specificity that is genuinely unique to digital infrastructure.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Accessibility — both technical (requires code literacy) and economic (gas costs, crypto requirement). Scale — the EVM computation limits constrain complexity. Critical discourse — the art critical establishment has not developed adequate vocabulary. Exhibition infrastructure — how do you display running code in a gallery? Audience — the conceptual sophistication limits the community to a very small group.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Almost everyone who is not a code-literate, crypto-native person with Ethereum and conceptual art background. Non-programmers cannot fully appreciate the work. Non-crypto users cannot own it. Traditional art audiences cannot access it without significant onboarding. The exclusion is near-total for the general public.
field_position.frontier_signal: Frontier — the leading edge of medium specificity in digital art. The 2025 academic attention (arXiv, ARTECH) suggests the concept is being recognized by broader discourse. The practice is small but conceptually influential. Not declining — growing in intellectual significance even as market remains niche.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Crypto art community (Twitter/X, Discord). Generative art collector networks. Academic publications. Tech media coverage of novel blockchain applications. Word of mouth among code-literate art practitioners. Not discoverable through mainstream art channels.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Low. The art exists on-chain regardless of attention. Collectors in this space are intrinsically motivated by conceptual interest rather than hype. The practice survived the NFT crash without significant disruption because it was never hype-dependent. Would survive if all social media disappeared — the art is on-chain.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Strongly intention-native. Declares and demonstrates that digital art can be executable code, not just files. This serves the field's structural need for medium specificity. No engagement optimization. The practice exists to prove a conceptual point about what art can be on blockchain.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Strong. On-chain code is inherently a commons contribution — anyone can read, study, and learn from it. The conceptual framework (art as running software) is a shared vocabulary contribution. Academic papers formalize the discourse. The practice demonstrates possibilities that benefit the entire field.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Ownership provenance through on-chain NFT records. Creative provenance through verifiable code authorship (deployer address, creation block, contract code). No provenance of meaning or critical reception — that lives off-chain.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Real-time and deep-historical simultaneously. The art runs in real-time (continuous computation) but is fixed at deployment (immutable code). Block numbers provide absolute temporal anchoring. Some works evolve based on blockchain time (block number, epoch). This is a unique temporal logic — perpetually present yet historically fixed.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Does not address field absences directly. But the practice itself was born from an absence — the recognition that NFTs were being treated as receipts for files rather than as executable programs. The movement addresses this specific absence by demonstrating the alternative.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence. Multiple valid approaches coexist — Pak's smart contract conceptualism, Material Protocol Arts' kinetic sculpture, 0xDEAFBEEF's audiovisual computation, Mathcastles' text-based worlds. No consensus on what runtime art should look like or mean, but a coherent shared commitment to code-as-medium.
coherence.contestability: High. Code is open and verifiable — any claim about what the art does can be checked. Artistic claims can be tested against the actual code. Smart contract behavior is deterministic and auditable. This is the most contestable art form — there is no gap between claim and verification.
coherence.forkability: Technically trivial (copy-paste the smart contract code). Practically meaningful — deploying a fork creates a new instance but not the original's provenance. The original's artistic significance comes from being first, being deployed by the artist, and having its specific on-chain history. Code is forkable; context and authorship are not.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The commitment to medium specificity — A(DAI) should be as native to its infrastructure as runtime art is to Ethereum. The principle that the system IS the art/intelligence, not a container for it. The on-chain persistence model as a reference for how A(DAI) should think about preservation. The open-by-nature design where the infrastructure is itself transparent and verifiable. The concept that ownership can mean owning a process rather than a file.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The extreme exclusivity that limits participation to code-literate crypto-natives. The absence of critical discourse and contextual framing. The emphasis on individual artistic authorship over collective intelligence. The gas-cost barriers that make interaction expensive. The immutability that prevents correction or evolution — A(DAI) must be able to update and evolve.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: Runtime art proves that digital art can be maximally medium-specific, but at the cost of maximal exclusion. A(DAI) must achieve medium specificity (being native to its own infrastructure) while remaining accessible to non-technical participants. Runtime art is immutable; A(DAI) must evolve. Runtime art is individual expression; A(DAI) is collective intelligence. The challenge: how to be as infrastructure-native as runtime art without being as exclusive.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Minimal for the art itself — code on-chain is protected by open-source norms and potentially by free speech protections. Smart contracts face growing regulatory scrutiny (OFAC sanctions on Tornado Cash set precedent). EU AI Act is not directly applicable (not AI). Securities regulation could apply if tokens are marketed as investments. The immutability of smart contracts creates compliance challenges — there is no way to update code to comply with new regulations.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: On-chain code is publicly visible but copyrighted by the deployer/artist. NFT ownership transfers the token but not the code copyright. Some artists use open-source licenses (MIT, CC0). The immutability and public visibility create a natural tension — the code is inspectable but legally protected. Pak's work raises questions about protocol-level authorship.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in. Collectors choose to purchase and interact. Viewers can inspect code freely. No opt-out issues — the art does not use external data or training data. The consent architecture is simple: own the token or don't.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Depends on Ethereum (for on-chain computation and storage). Some projects on other EVM chains. No platform dependency beyond the blockchain itself — this is the most platform-independent art form. If OpenSea or any marketplace disappears, the art continues to exist and compute on-chain. Dependency on web browsers for rendering layer (JavaScript execution).
ecosystem.network_effects: Limited direct network effects — each project is relatively independent. Indirect network effects through shared collector community, shared critical discourse, and shared infrastructure (Ethereum). The movement benefits from Ethereum's network effects (developer tools, wallet infrastructure, marketplace access).
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Stable through the crash. The conceptual value proposition (code as art) is not tied to market speculation. Collector base was never hype-driven. Academic interest (2025 papers) suggests growing intellectual recognition even as market volumes remain modest. Trajectory: stable niche with growing critical significance. Terraforms and early on-chain projects have appreciated in collector esteem even as broader NFT market declined.
